A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CellCLIP and contain the complete 23-page paper, including appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison; pages 3–23 are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, biological relationship recovery, computational timing and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical evaluations and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical per-channel feature extraction, attention pooling, CrossChannelFormer architecture, BERT perturbation encoding and CWCL/CLIP training objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Bray et al., CP-JUMP1 and RxRx3-core datasets for cross-modal retrieval, replicate detection, sister perturbation matching and gene relationship recovery. No data or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout. Table 1 retains the same CLOOME and MolPhenix* variants; Table 3 retains its additional OpenPhenom-S/16 and ViT-L/16 comparisons, and appendix comparator sets also match.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–E report identical splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model configurations and evaluation procedures. No experimental settings are revised or newly introduced.

E4.justification: Table 2 and Appendix A retain the same encoder, pooling and contrastive-loss ablations, together with the same backbone and retrieval-threshold analyses. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Reporting of means and standard deviations across random seeds is unchanged. Appendix C.2.1 retains the same 100,000-shuffle permutation testing and multiple-comparison correction; no run-count or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, rankings and reported findings in Tables 1–3, Tables S.1–S.6 and Figure S.1 are identical, including retrieval performance, biological recovery and computational timing results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14) and their accompanying mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, derivations or proofs relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about text-based perturbation representation, CrossChannelFormer, retrieval performance and computational efficiency. The added code-access sentence does not change the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including explanations of pooling and channel reasoning, weak cross-class matching, the need for wet-lab validation and constraints from proprietary datasets and models.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct CellCLIP GitHub repository link in the abstract for reproducing experiments; v1 contains no corresponding CellCLIP code-access link. Implementation, hardware and training details remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: The same 45 references and research-positioning passages are retained. Relationships to CLOOME, MolPhenix, channel-aware vision models and other prior work are unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The added sentence contains the grammatical slip 'Code for our reproducing our experiments'; existing prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer abstract changes line wrapping and pushes two introduction lines from page 1 onto page 2. All figures, tables and captions remain unchanged, and pages 3–23 have identical rendered layouts.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer supplies concrete code-access guidance absent from v1, modestly improving the paper's usefulness for reproduction despite the sentence's grammatical slip. Methods, evidence and conclusions remain unchanged. This judgment concerns the documented access information; the PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or functionality.
